newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cricket-Heavy late hitting boosts Pakistan innings.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Heavy late hitting boosts Pakistan innings.

text.p: Lusty hitting late in the innings helped Pakistan overcome a sluggish start to post 257 for seven in their World Series Cup limited-overs match against West Indies on Friday.
Number four batsman Ijaz Ahmed was the cornerstone of the innings, hitting three sixes and six fours in a knock of 94 before being run out in the final stages.

Most of Ijaz's runs were scored from a flurry of boundaries in the last 12 overs, boosting Pakistan's total after they had looked in danger of getting bogged down in the face of accurate West Indies slow bowling.

The injection of 19-year-old spin bowler Shahid Afridi up the order proved the trigger for the late explosion of runs. Shahid appeared in the 39th over at the fall of the third wicket with the score on 151.
Shahid, who burst on to the world cricketing stage with a century against Sri Lanka late last year, scored 29 runs off 19 balls, including one huge six over long on.
Pakistan had looked tentative earlier on against the accurate slow bowling of Jimmy Adams and Carl Hooper on a bouncing and sometimes turning pitch.
Pakistan scored just 45 runs in the first 15 overs but Ijaz launched into the previously economical Adams in the 38th over, from which he scored 19 runs including two fours and a six.
Slipshod fielding from a West Indies team which appeared to feel the oppressive Perth heat also helped Pakistan.
Their most costly error came just before Pakistan accelerated, when wicket-keeper Junior Murray missed a clear stumping chance to dismiss Ijaz when he was on 36.
Pakistan were in a good position to win the match given their hefty total and a surfeit of spin bowlers likely to extract bounce and turn from the WACA pitch.
